# Plan: The Yantra App and the Drshya Design System

## 1. Overview

Yantra is CLI-only today. This plan builds the **Yantra app**: a local graphical app opened by
`yantra ui` in a Chrome app window, styled by **Drshya**, Yantra's own design system, and held level
with the CLI by construction. The design source is [`ui_brainstorm.md`](./ui_brainstorm.md)
(Session 5); the visual reference is
[Yantra Interface Study 01](https://claude.ai/artifact/46XfRuWQyypjqhS3B9xPQB), with the **Ion**
accent chosen.

The plan has three parts:

1. **Foundations that also improve the CLI.** A declarative command registry, one sequence-numbered
   run-event stream, and run leases with a per-run local socket. These are protocol and core work. The
   CLI benefits on its own: a killed run is no longer "running" forever, and every surface renders
   the same events.
2. **A reliable local app host.** `yantra ui` starts a supervisor process that serves the app on
   `127.0.0.1`, runs tasks as **detached CLI worker processes** (two at a time, the rest queued), and
   reattaches to them after any crash. The scheduler daemon is untouched and stays hard zero-LLM
   (memory → Architecture).
3. **The app.** Drshya (`packages/ui`) and `apps/web`: read surfaces for every run, a live run screen
   for `ask`/`research`/`do`/`run`, interventions with an Inbox, the live browser view, a command
   palette, and generated surfaces so every remaining command is usable on day one.

**In scope:** FEAT-061 to FEAT-071. **Explicitly deferred to Phase 2** and documented in
[§13](#13-phase-2-deferred-and-documented): live takeover (solving a captcha or login yourself in
the live view), an `ask_user` tool for missing information, desktop notifications for finished or
failed runs, live viewing of CLI-launched runs, and the bespoke studios (workflows, recorder,
templates, schedules, usage, provenance graph).

## 3. Tech Stack Additions

The canonical stack is in `memory.md` → Tech Stack. These are additions for this plan. Per memory
(Dependencies), **the user approves each new dependency before it is pinned**; Feature specs pin
exact current stable versions at that point.

| Component                | Technology                                                                                                        | Justification                                                                                                                                    |
| ------------------------ | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| UI runtime               | `react`, `react-dom` (19.x)                                                                                       | Largest accessible-primitive ecosystem; React Aria is React-only. Session 1 direction.                                                           |
| Build                    | `vite`, `@vitejs/plugin-react`                                                                                    | Fast static build for a localhost app; no SSR need, so no Next.js.                                                                               |
| Routing and read caching | `@tanstack/react-router`, `@tanstack/react-query`                                                                 | Type-safe file routes; cache, dedupe and invalidation for in-process reads.                                                                      |
| Primitives               | `react-aria-components`                                                                                           | Broadest accessible set: virtualized Table and GridList, Tree, drag and drop, DatePicker, i18n. State exposed as data attributes. User decision. |
| Styling                  | `tailwindcss` v4, `@tailwindcss/vite`, `tailwindcss-react-aria-components`, `tailwind-variants`, `tailwind-merge` | CSS-first `@theme` tokens; React Aria state variants; multi-slot component variants.                                                             |
| Icons                    | `lucide-react`                                                                                                    | ISC; used only behind the Drshya semantic icon registry.                                                                                         |
| Fonts                    | `@fontsource-variable/archivo`, `@fontsource-variable/martian-mono`                                               | Self-hosted (OFL); a local-first app makes no third-party requests.                                                                              |
| Markdown in Briefs       | `react-markdown` with `remark-gfm`, raw HTML disabled                                                             | Brief `sections[].body_md` and template documents; no `dangerouslySetInnerHTML`.                                                                 |
| WebSocket server         | `ws`                                                                                                              | Node 24 has no built-in WebSocket server. HTTP uses `node:http`; run sockets use `node:net`.                                                     |
| Component tests          | `@testing-library/react` (with the repo's existing jsdom)                                                         | Instrument behavior tests under Vitest.                                                                                                          |
| Visual regression        | `pixelmatch`, `pngjs`                                                                                             | Screenshots taken with the existing `puppeteer-core`; no second browser driver.                                                                  |

**Deliberately not added:** Storybook (an in-app gallery route suffices), Playwright (puppeteer-core
already drives Chrome), Motion (CSS and View Transitions cover the MVP), a state-management

## 4. Decisions

Recorded at the planning checkpoints of 2026-11-02.

- **D1 — Separate app host; the daemon is unchanged.** Memory makes scheduled and daemon runs hard
  zero-LLM, and `daemon-runtime.ts` enforces it. Serving the app from the daemon would make `do` and
  agentic research impossible from the app. `yantra ui` therefore starts its own host for attended
  work. The app still shows schedules and parked runs (read from disk, daemon state via
  `FileDaemonLock.probe()`) and resolves parked runs through the `confirm` command.
- **D2 — Supervisor plus CLI workers; reads in-process.** The host never executes a task. Run-class
  and mutating commands run as worker processes that execute the **same command handler with the
  same argv** as the terminal, so the CLI twin is literally the command that ran. Reads (runs,
  Briefs, audit, config, schedules) use core read functions in the host process. **One exception:**
  credential writes run in-process through the core keychain function `secret set` uses, so a secret
  never appears in a process argument list.
- **D3 — Detached workers own a per-run socket; any host can reattach.** Workers are spawned
  detached and outlive the host. Each worker serves its run on a local socket recorded in an
  owner-only lease. A restarted host finds live leases, reconnects with the run token, replays from
  `run-events.jsonl`, then follows live. The fork IPC channel was rejected because it dies with the
  parent.
- **D4 — Two concurrent run-class workers; the rest queue.** The limit counts live leases of
  app-launched runs, so a restarted host still respects it. CLI-launched runs are shown but not
  throttled. The queue is persisted; after a host restart, queued items show as **Not started**
  with Start and Discard, and never start on their own.
- **D5 — Human intervention with no host attached.** The worker records the intervention, sends a
  desktop "needs you" notification itself, and keeps waiting under an **attendance ceiling of 15
  minutes** of no attached host. A host that attaches in time shows it at once. On expiry the
  request fails closed and the run exits cleanly as a **handoff** (exit 4) with the pending item
  recorded. The ceiling **never extends** existing bounds: the effective wait is the minimum of the
  request's `timeout_ms`, `agent.confirm_timeout` (agentic runs, default 3 minutes), the run's
  remaining wall clock, and the attendance ceiling.
- **D6 — Host death does not stop runs.** Workers continue and try to complete; only an
  intervention falls back to D5.
- **D7 — Interrupted runs reuse existing vocabulary.** A run whose owner died is reconciled to status
  `aborted` with termination reason `interrupted`, not a new status value, so older readers of run
  artifacts stay valid (memory → General, artifact compatibility).
- **D8 — Design decisions carried from the brainstorm.** Ion accent; Chrome app window; React Aria
  Components; design system name **Drshya**, published as package `@yantra/ui`; glass for controls
  only, with Solid mode; command registry in `@yantra/protocol`, generating commander (not derived
  from it); gallery as an in-app development route.
- **D9 — Phase 2 is explicit.** Live takeover, `ask_user`, finished/failed desktop notifications,
  live viewing of CLI runs and the bespoke studios are documented in §13 with what the MVP lays
  down for each. Desktop notifications for **"needs you"** items stay in the MVP, because D5 depends
  on them and the existing `SinkNotifier` already provides them.
- **D10 — UI window browser.** The app window prefers an installed system Chromium that supports
  `--app` (Chrome, then Edge), because Chrome for Testing shows a "for automated testing only"
  infobar. It falls back to the resolved Yantra browser, then to printing the URL. The window always
  uses its own profile and never the automation instance or an automation profile.

## 5. Evidence

Facts from the codebase that shaped the decisions:

- `apps/cli/src/commands/daemon-runtime.ts:109,153`: daemon fires and parked-run resumes never open
  a model session (D1).
- `apps/cli/src/commands/run.ts:171-174`: a confirmation gateway is wired only on a TTY without
  `--json`, so "spawn `--json` and parse stdout" cannot answer approvals (D2).
- `packages/core/src/workflow/replay/run-orchestrator.ts:388`: the manifest is set to `running` and
  nothing detects a dead owner (FEAT-064).
- `packages/agent/src/runtime/orchestrator.ts:1262,1327`: an agentic handoff (captcha, bot wall,
  MFA, site restriction) is terminal with `blocker` and `safestNextAction` (FEAT-068).
- `packages/agent/src/runtime/connector.ts`: `AgentProgressEvent` lives in `@yantra/agent`, while
  `TaskEvent` lives in protocol (FEAT-063).
- `packages/agent/src/runtime/confirmation-bridge.ts:75-89`: non-interactive connectors time out at
  once; interactive waits are bounded by `agent.confirm_timeout` and wall clock (D5).
- `packages/protocol/src/schemas/confirmation.ts`: `ConfirmationDecidedBy` is the closed enum
  `user_interactive | user_cli_confirm | timeout` (FEAT-068 adds `user_app`).
- `packages/core/src/scheduler/notify.ts`: `SinkNotifier` writes `notifications.jsonl` and sends a
  best-effort desktop notification (FEAT-068).
- `apps/cli/src/connector-io.ts`: `ConnectorId` already includes `'web'`.

## 6. Interface Design

### CLI surface

- **`yantra ui [--print] [--json]`** (new). Starts the app host if none is live, then opens the app
  window with a fresh launch code. `--print` prints the URL instead of opening a window (same
  spelling as `open --print`). `--json` emits `{schemaVersion, url, port, hostPid, reused}`. Exit
  codes: 0 opened or printed; 3 environment (no usable Chromium and no `--print`, port bind
  failure, lock contention); 1 validation.
- **`yantra confirm <run-id> <grant|deny>`** (extended). Also resolves a **live** intervention of an
  app- or CLI-launched run through that run's socket, recorded as `decided_by: user_cli_confirm`.
  Parked scheduled runs behave as today.
- **`yantra prefs set ui.theme|ui.density|ui.surfaces`** (new keys in `profile.yaml`): `theme` is
  `system|light|dark`; `density` is `comfort|compact` (compact is accepted but renders as comfort
  until Phase 2); `surfaces` is `glass|solid`.
- **No other user-visible change.** The worker entry point is internal (`apps/cli/dist/worker.js`)
  and is not a flag, per the flag-vocabulary rule in memory.

### Execution classes (registry field `execution`)

| Class               | Runs where                                                      | Examples                                                                                                                                                                               | Counts toward the limit of 2 |
| ------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------- |
| `read`              | Host, in-process, read-only core functions                      | `list`, `show`, `audit`, `report`, `usage`, `schedules`, `config get/list/path/validate`, `profile`, `model list`, `sites list`, `template list/show`, `daemon status`, `browser list` | No                           |
| `mutate`            | Short-lived worker                                              | `config set/unset/data-dir`, `prefs set`, `model add/rm/default`, `sites add/remove`, `template new/save/remove/lint`, `lint`, `schedule`, `unschedule`, `confirm`                     | No                           |
| `run`               | Detached worker with lease and socket                           | `ask`, `research`, `do`, `run`, `resume`, `browser check`                                                                                                                              | Yes                          |
| `exclusive`         | Detached worker; refuses while any run is live (existing rules) | `browser install`, `browser update`                                                                                                                                                    | Blocks the queue             |
| `in-process-secure` | Host, in-process                                                | `secret set/rm` (value never in argv), `secret list` (names only)                                                                                                                      | No                           |

`doctor` is `read` without `--smoke` and `run` with it.

### Run socket protocol (worker ↔ host or `yantra confirm`)

Newline-delimited JSON over `node:net`; binary screencast frames are length-prefixed on the same
connection (FEAT-069). Every message is a Zod schema in protocol, carrying `channel_version`.

| Direction       | Message                                              | Purpose                                                                            |
| --------------- | ---------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| client → worker | `hello {token, client: 'app-host' \| 'cli-confirm'}` | Authenticate with the run token from the owner-only lease                          |
| client → worker | `subscribe {from_seq}`                               | Replay from `run-events.jsonl`, then live                                          |
| worker → client | `event {seq, event: RunEvent}`                       | Ordered, gap-free stream                                                           |
| worker → client | `heartbeat {at}`                                     | Liveness every 5 s                                                                 |
| client → worker | `intervention.answer {intervention_id, decision}`    | Resolve consent; the worker stamps `decided_by` from the authenticated client kind |
| client → worker | `cancel {reason}`                                    | Same clean-abort path as `SIGINT`                                                  |
| client → worker | `frames.start` / `frames.stop` / `frame.ack {n}`     | Screencast flow control (FEAT-069)                                                 |

### Host control socket

An owner-only local socket beside the host lock. `yantra ui` uses it to request `open-window`
(the host mints a single-use launch code) and `status`.

### App ↔ host

- **HTTP:** `GET /` and static assets; `POST /session` exchanges the launch code for the session
  cookie; `GET /artifacts/<run-id>/<path>` streams run files to an authenticated session. Nothing
  else.
- **WebSocket, JSON-RPC 2.0** (one connection per window):
  - `command.invoke {invocation}` → `{run_id}` for `run`/`exclusive` classes or a result for
    `mutate`. `invocation` is the registry's `CommandInvocation` (command path plus argv), the same
    object the CLI twin renders.
  - `command.cancel {run_id}`, `queue.list`, `queue.start {id}`, `queue.discard {id}`.
  - `read.<name>` for each `read`-class command; results use that command's `--json` output schema.
  - `run.subscribe {run_id, from_seq}` → notifications `run.event {seq, event}`; `runs.subscribe` →
    `runs.changed`; `interventions.subscribe` → `intervention.changed`.
  - `intervention.answer {intervention_id, decision}`.
  - `frames.subscribe {run_id}` (FEAT-069; binary frames on the same socket).
  - `secret.set {key}` with the value sent once in the request body, never echoed; `secret.rm`;
    `secret.list` (names only).

### Surfaces and flow

`Mission` (start page: composer, live cockpit) · `Ledger` (all runs) → `Brief` / `Audit` per run ·
`Inbox` (badge in the top bar; the Bindu turns Rani when non-empty) · `Settings` (Installation,
Preferences, Models, Credentials, Browser, Sites, Data) · `Health` · `Workflows`, `Templates`,
`Schedules`, `Usage` as generated surfaces in the MVP · `/gallery` in development builds only.
`Ctrl/Cmd+K` opens the palette everywhere. The full CLI → surface map is in
[`ui_brainstorm.md` §Information Architecture](./ui_brainstorm.md); FEAT-070 makes it a test.

### Artifacts (all additive)

- Per run: `runs/<id>/lease.json` (owner-only; deleted on clean exit), `runs/<id>/run-events.jsonl`
  (sequence-numbered `RunEvent`s), `runs/<id>/interventions.jsonl` (intervention lifecycle; consent
  entries reference the existing `confirmations.jsonl` records).
- Host state under `<data-dir>/ui/`: `host.lock` (PID, port, control-socket address), `queue.json`,
  `host.log`, `chrome-profile/`. Unix sockets live in a short owner-only directory (socket paths
  are length-limited, about 104 bytes on macOS); Windows uses named pipes. **Every path comes from
  `packages/core/src/browser/paths.ts`** (memory → Project Structure).
- Existing files (`events.jsonl`, `runtime.jsonl`, `tool-calls.jsonl`, `manifest.json`,
  `brief.*`, `confirmations.jsonl`) keep their shapes.

### Protocol additions

`CommandRegistry` and `CommandInvocation`; `RunEvent`; `Intervention`; `RunLease`; run-socket and
host-control messages; app RPC messages; `ConfirmationDecidedBy` gains `user_app`.

## 7. Security Considerations

Standing rules are in `memory.md` → Security. Plan-specific concerns:

- **Localhost is reachable from any web page.** The host binds `127.0.0.1` only, on a random port.
  `yantra ui` passes a single-use launch code in the URL **fragment** (never in a request line, so
  never logged). `POST /session` exchanges it for an `HttpOnly; SameSite=Strict; Path=/` cookie.
  Every request and WebSocket upgrade requires `Host` to be exactly `127.0.0.1:<port>` or
  `localhost:<port>` (defeats DNS rebinding); every mutation and upgrade requires the exact app
  `Origin`. No CORS headers. A strict `Content-Security-Policy` (`default-src 'self'`) and no
  third-party requests.
- **Run sockets are authenticated by token, not only by OS permissions.** POSIX sockets sit in an
  owner-only (0700) directory with 0600 files. Windows named pipes created by Node get a default
  security descriptor that can grant read access beyond the owner, so **the first message must carry
  the run token** from the owner-only lease, pipe names include unguessable random suffixes, and
  unauthenticated connections are closed without a reply.
- **Secrets never travel toward the app.** Credential writes run in-process (D2), values never go
  in argv, and responses list names only. A canary-secret test scans every WebSocket message, HTTP
  response, run-socket message, `run-events.jsonl` and `host.log`.
- **Consent provenance stays unforgeable.** `decided_by: user_app` is produced only by the worker,
  from an `intervention.answer` that arrived over an authenticated host connection after the app's
  hold gesture. `user_cli_confirm` is stamped for `yantra confirm` connections. There is still no
  agent variant.
- **Screencast privacy (FEAT-069).** Task page only; frames are never written to disk and never sent
  to the model, so they fall outside the `context.screenshots` grant. Under the sensitive-screen
  latch the **worker stops sending frames**; this is not a client-side blur. Document this in
  `docs/features/safety-and-privacy.md`.
- **Artifact serving.** Paths resolve with `realpath` and must stay inside the runs root;
  `Content-Type` comes from an extension allowlist; `X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff`; HTML
  artifacts (`brief.html`, `document.html`) are served as downloads, never rendered. The app renders
  Briefs from `brief.json`.
- **Page-derived text is untrusted.** Titles, quotes, URLs and model text render through React
  escaping and a markdown renderer with raw HTML disabled. External links carry
  `rel="noopener noreferrer"`.
- **The app window is not an automation target.** It runs in a dedicated profile with no remote
  debugging port, separate from every automation browser and profile (D10).

## 8. Architecture & Design (Plan-Specific)

### Process model

```
yantra ui ──control socket──► App host  (one per machine: <data-dir>/ui/host.lock)
                                 │  HTTP + WebSocket on 127.0.0.1 ◄──── Chrome --app window
                                 │  reads in-process (core read functions)
                                 │  supervisor: queue, limit 2, spawns detached workers
                                 ▼
             ┌────────── worker (detached) = CLI command handler + WorkerConnector
             │              lease.json · run socket · run-events.jsonl · run artifacts
             └────────── worker (detached) …
yantra <cmd> in a terminal: same handler + terminal connector; also writes lease.json and serves a run socket
yantra daemon: unchanged, hard zero-LLM; the app reads its state and resolves parked runs via `confirm`
```

### Dependency direction

`protocol → core → agent → cli` is unchanged. `packages/ui` depends on `@yantra/protocol` **for
types only** and never imports core, agent or Node built-ins. `apps/web` depends on `@yantra/ui`
and `@yantra/protocol`. `apps/cli` embeds the built `apps/web/dist` as static files at build time;
it does not import web code. Turbo orders `apps/web#build` before `apps/cli#build`.

### Run lifecycle

`queued → starting → running ⇄ waiting-for-you → fulfilled | partial | handoff | failed | aborted`,
where `aborted` carries `interrupted` when reconciliation found a dead owner (D7). The app shows the
CLI's words verbatim.

### Reliability matrix

| Failure                  | Behavior                                                                                                                                                        |
| ------------------------ | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Worker crashes           | Host records the exit code; the run's terminal event is written by reconciliation if the worker could not write it; the host keeps serving                      |
| Worker hangs             | No heartbeat for 30 s → shown as **Stalled** with Stop                                                                                                          |
| User stops a run         | `cancel` over the socket → clean abort; after a 10 s grace, `SIGTERM`, then kill; Chrome reaped by recorded PIDs                                                |
| App window closes        | Workers continue; the host exits after 10 minutes with no window and no queued items; `yantra ui` reattaches                                                    |
| Browser connection drops | App reconnects with backoff, resubscribes `from_seq`; no gaps, no duplicates                                                                                    |
| Host crashes             | Workers continue (D6); interventions follow D5; the next host reattaches by lease                                                                               |
| Any owner dies           | Startup reconciliation (host start, CLI run start, `yantra list`) marks dead-owner `running` runs `aborted`/`interrupted`                                       |
| Recovery                 | Workflow runs offer **Resume** (checkpoints); agentic runs offer **Run again** with the same `CommandInvocation`, because a provider session cannot be reopened |

### Intervention wait computation

Effective wait = min(`request.timeout_ms`, `agent.confirm_timeout` for agentic runs, remaining wall
clock, attendance ceiling). The attendance ceiling runs only while **no** authenticated host is
attached to the run socket. It starts when an intervention is raised with no host attached, or when
the last host detaches while one is pending. It resets on attach. Expiry resolves the request as
`timed_out` (`decided_by: timeout`), so the run ends as a handoff. A workflow run attended in the app
waits as long as it would on a terminal; agentic waits stay bounded as today (memory → Error
Handling).

### One event stream, many consumers

`RunEvent` is emitted once through `ConnectorIO`. Consumers are the terminal renderer, the JSON
renderer, `run-events.jsonl` and the run socket. Instruments switch over the union with compile-time
exhaustiveness. Kinds without a bespoke instrument are routed explicitly to `EventInspector`.

### Sequencing

1. **FEAT-061** and **FEAT-062** can run in parallel. FEAT-063 can start alongside them.
2. **FEAT-064** after FEAT-063 (the socket streams `RunEvent`s).
3. **FEAT-065** after FEAT-061, FEAT-062 and FEAT-064.
4. **FEAT-066** after FEAT-065. **FEAT-069 task 1** (the readability and performance spike) may run
   any time after FEAT-064 and should run early, because it tests the riskiest assumption.
5. **FEAT-067** after FEAT-063 and FEAT-066; **FEAT-068** after FEAT-067.
6. **FEAT-069** (rest) after FEAT-067; **FEAT-070** after FEAT-062, FEAT-065 and FEAT-066;
   **FEAT-071** after FEAT-070.

### Compatibility

Existing artifacts are unchanged; new files are additive. CLI-visible changes are limited to: the
new `yantra ui` command, `confirm` resolving live interventions, the `ui.*` preference keys, and
dead-owner runs showing as `aborted` (interrupted) instead of `running`. `--help` output is
byte-identical after FEAT-062.

### Risks

| Risk                                                    | Mitigation                                                                                                                                                                                 |
| ------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| Registry extraction touches ~30 commands and 98 options | Migrate command by command; a `--help` snapshot suite per command proves no CLI change; the parity test tolerates unmigrated commands only through a dated allowlist that FEAT-070 empties |
| Glass over a live screencast is slow or illegible       | FEAT-069 task 1 spike before the HUD is built; automatic Solid fallback over the frame-time budget; Solid preference always available                                                      |
| Windows named-pipe permissions                          | Token authentication is mandatory (§7); a Windows CI job covers pipes                                                                                                                      |
| Detached processes on three OSes                        | One spawn helper with per-OS tests (detached, no inherited stdio, `windowsHide`)                                                                                                           |
| Two execution hosts diverge                             | There is one handler; worker and terminal differ only in connector. Shared e2e scenarios run both ways                                                                                     |
| Design perfectionism delays value                       | Read surfaces ship first; generated surfaces give every command a usable view before bespoke work                                                                                          |

## 9. Coding Standards (Plan-Specific Overrides)

Memory's standards apply. Additions for UI code:

- **Styling only through Drshya semantic utilities.** No raw palette utilities (`bg-blue-500`), no
  arbitrary color values, no hex or `oklch()` literals in components. Enforced by a lint rule in
  `packages/ui` and `apps/web`. Inline `style` is allowed only for CSS custom properties carrying
  data (for example a gauge's `--v`).
- **Icons only from the semantic registry**; importing `lucide-react` outside the registry is a lint
  error.
- **Interactive elements come from Drshya primitives** built on React Aria. No `div` buttons or
  hand-rolled menus, dialogs or listboxes.
- **`packages/ui` imports no Node built-ins and nothing from `@yantra/core` or `@yantra/agent`**
  (import-boundary lint, mirroring memory's `core`/`agent` boundary rule).
- **Function components and hooks only.** Live state comes from a `useSyncExternalStore` store over
  the event stream; no global singletons (memory → Architecture, explicit dependency injection).
- **Product words are the CLI's words.** Outcome words, condition statuses and error text are
  rendered verbatim from protocol values; the UI never invents synonyms.
- Tests live in mirrored `tests/` directories as everywhere else; `.tsx` files are linted and
  type-checked repo-wide (memory → Testing: the repo-wide gate is the gate).

## 10. Testing Strategy (Plan-Specific)

Memory's testing rules apply, including: e2e and CLI suites resolve `@yantra/core` from built
`dist/`, real-Chrome cases need their own timeouts, count work on stepped clocks, and the repo-wide
lint and typecheck are the gate.

- **Unit (Vitest):** registry schemas and generation; argv parse/format round-trip for every
  registered command; `RunEvent` and `Intervention` schemas; lease, heartbeat and reconciliation;
  attendance-ceiling computation on a stepped clock; queue persistence; Host/Origin/cookie
  middleware.
- **`--help` snapshot suite (FEAT-062):** byte-identical help for every command before and after
  generation.
- **Component tests:** every instrument with Testing Library over jsdom, including exhaustive
  `RunEvent` routing.
- **Visual regression:** the `/gallery` route captured with puppeteer-core in light and dark ×
  Glass and Solid; `pixelmatch` thresholds. Goldens update only through an explicit script, and the
  formatter never runs over them (memory → no blanket prettier on goldens).
- **Contrast:** every semantic text/background pairing, including both Ion fills, ≥ 4.5:1;
  glass text sampled over light, dark and busy backdrops.
- **Security suite (merge gate for FEAT-065 onward):** missing or replayed launch code; foreign
  `Origin`; rebinding `Host`; cross-site form POST; unauthenticated run-socket connection;
  artifact path traversal; canary secret absent from every channel and file listed in §7.
- **Reliability e2e:** kill a worker mid-run; kill the host mid-run (the worker completes; a new
  host reattaches and replays with no gaps or duplicates); kill both (reconciliation reports
  `aborted`/`interrupted`); an intervention with no host expires at the ceiling (stepped clock) and
  the run exits 4 with the item recorded; the limit of 2 holds across a host restart; queued items
  show **Not started** after a restart.
- **App e2e** (puppeteer-core driving the app window): `ask --no-llm` from the composer to the
  Brief; a scripted fake-provider `do` with a consent request answered by the hold gesture; Ledger
  → Audit; `yantra confirm` resolving an app-run intervention. Runs in the existing
  `LLM_PROVIDER=none` dimension where applicable.
- **Parity test (FEAT-070):** fails on any registry command, `RunEvent` kind or artifact type
  without a mapping or written exemption.
- **Cross-platform:** run sockets and detached spawn on Windows, macOS and Linux CI.
- **Performance:** event latency worker → app p95 < 150 ms on a replayed run; screencast ≥ 5 fps
  with the app main thread under 15% of one core (FEAT-069).

## 11. Logging Strategy (Plan-Specific)

Memory's logging rules apply (structured Pino, never secrets).

- **Host log** (`<data-dir>/ui/host.log`): host start and stop, worker spawn with run id and
  execution class, worker exit code, attach and reattach, reconciliation decisions, queue
  transitions, and security rejections as counts with the rejected `Origin` host. **Never** launch
  codes, cookies, run tokens, socket addresses with tokens, secret values or screencast frames.
- **Runs:** `runtime.jsonl` gains projections for `intervention_raised`, `intervention_resolved`
  (kind, decided_by, waited ms; no free text beyond the sanitized summary), `channel_attached` and
  `channel_detached` (client kind only), and `attendance_ceiling_expired`.
- Heartbeats are not logged individually; a stall is logged once when detected.

## 12. Feature Scope and Acceptance

### FEAT-061: Drshya Foundations

**Scope.** Create `packages/ui` (`@yantra/ui`):

- Tokens in Tailwind v4 `@theme` across three tiers:
  - primitive: fog ramp, Ion, Jade, Amber, Crimson, Rani;
  - semantic: `bg`, `surface`, `sunken`, `ink`/`ink-2`/`ink-3`, `rule`/`rule-strong`, `accent`,
    `on-accent`, `accent-ink`, `signal-*`, `glass-*`;
  - component knobs.
- Values come from `ui_brainstorm.md` §Color, with Ion's two fills.
- Light and dark themes, through `prefers-color-scheme` plus `data-theme`. Comfort density. Solid
  mode through `data-surfaces` and `prefers-reduced-transparency`.
- The glass recipe and its scrim floor.
- The type scale, with self-hosted Archivo (widths 100 to 125) and Martian Mono (width 87.5).
- Radius, space and motion tokens; reduced motion honored.
- The semantic icon registry and the six custom glyphs on Lucide's grid.
- Primitives on React Aria Components: Button, Link, TextField, NumberField, Checkbox, Switch,
  Select, ComboBox, Dialog, Popover, Menu, Tabs, Table (virtualized), Toast, Tooltip, Disclosure.
- The raw-color and icon-import lint rules.
- A `/gallery` development route (hosted by `apps/web` once it exists; a standalone Vite harness
  before that) and the screenshot harness.

**Acceptance.** Every primitive renders in the gallery in light and dark, Glass and Solid, with
visual baselines committed. Every text pairing passes the contrast test, including Ion on both
themes. Lint fails on a raw palette utility or a direct `lucide-react` import in a component. The
package has no import from core, agent or Node built-ins. Keyboard focus is visible everywhere (Ion
ring).

### FEAT-062: Command Registry

**Scope.** A Zod-described declarative registry in `@yantra/protocol`. For each command and
subcommand it records:

- the path and arguments;
- options with type, default, the precedence chain (flag > env > preference > default, naming the
  env var and preference key), applicability and help text;
- the `execution` class, the exit codes, and the `--json` output schema reference.

The CLI's commander tree is generated from it, command by command, with handlers bound by command
path. `CommandInvocation` (path plus argv) gets `parse` and `format` functions. The CLI twin and the
palette use them. A worker reproduces a run from them.

**Acceptance.** `--help` for every command is byte-identical before and after (snapshot suite).
Every registered command round-trips `format(parse(argv))`. No command registers an option it
cannot act on (memory → General; a test asserts each option has a consumer). Unmigrated commands
appear only on a dated allowlist.

### FEAT-063: Unified Run-Event Stream

**Scope.**

- A `RunEvent` union in `@yantra/protocol` with `schema_version`. It covers:
  - the existing `TaskEvent` kinds;
  - the `AgentProgressEvent` variants, promoted from `@yantra/agent` and re-exported there for
    compatibility (`recovery`, `progress`, `assistant_text`, `tool_started`, `tool_finished`,
    `contract_declared`, `capability_gap`);
  - new variants: `goal_echo`, `budget_snapshot`, `artifact_saved`, `intervention_raised`,
    `intervention_resolved`, `run_outcome`;
  - deterministic `ask`/`research` phase events (search, per-source fetch result, extract,
    synthesize), so a `--no-llm` run is visible live.
- `ConnectorIO` emits `RunEvent`s.
- A writer appends every event with a monotonic `seq` to `run-events.jsonl`.
- The terminal and JSON renderers consume the union; their output does not change.

**Acceptance.** Every live event a CLI run shows today has a `RunEvent` counterpart. `seq` is gap-free
per run. Terminal and `--json` output for existing golden scenarios is unchanged. Existing artifact
files are unchanged. The events are already sanitized and bounded; a canary secret never appears in
`run-events.jsonl`.

### FEAT-064: Run Leases, Run Channel & Reconciliation

**Scope.**

- **Lease.** On run start every run, from a terminal or an app worker, writes an owner-only
  `lease.json` containing the PID, process start time, socket address, a random 256-bit token,
  heartbeat time and execution class. The lease is removed on clean exit.
- **Run socket.** Each run serves the §6 run socket protocol: replay from `run-events.jsonl` then
  live, `intervention.answer`, `cancel`, and heartbeat.
- **Worker.** The detached worker entry `apps/cli/dist/worker.js` runs a registry `CommandInvocation`
  through the same handler with a `WorkerConnector`. The worker is interactive for consent while a
  client is attached or the attendance ceiling is open.
- **Spawn helper.** One cross-platform helper spawns workers detached, with no inherited stdio and
  `windowsHide`.
- **Reconciliation.** Dead-owner `running` runs become `aborted` with `interrupted` (D7). Liveness is
  checked by PID plus start time, so a reused PID is not mistaken for the owner. Reconciliation runs
  at host start, at CLI run start and in `yantra list`.
- **Chrome cleanup.** Chrome launched by a dead worker is reaped through its recorded PIDs.
- **Data-dir guard.** `config data-dir` refuses while live leases or a host lock exist, alongside the
  existing daemon check.

**Acceptance.**

- Killing a run's process leaves it reported as `aborted`/`interrupted` on the next reconciliation.
- A reused PID is not treated as the owner.
- A second client can attach, replay and follow with no gaps or duplicates.
- An unauthenticated socket client receives nothing.
- `cancel` behaves exactly like `SIGINT`.
- All of the above pass on Windows (named pipes) and POSIX (sockets).

### FEAT-065: App Host & `yantra ui`

**Scope.**

- **Command.** `yantra ui` (§6).
- **Host.** A single-instance host with `host.lock` and a control socket, serving HTTP and WebSocket
  JSON-RPC on `127.0.0.1`.
- **Sessions and security.** The launch-code exchange and session cookie, Host/Origin enforcement,
  CSP, and authenticated artifact streaming with path containment.
- **Supervisor.**
  - Executes `run`/`exclusive`/`mutate` invocations as workers, with a limit of 2 on run-class
    leases and a persisted `queue.json` (D4).
  - Reattaches to live leases at start.
  - Resubscribes browser connections `from_seq`.
  - Exits after 10 minutes idle.
- **Reads.** In-process `read.*` methods that return each command's `--json` schema.
- **Preferences.** `ui.theme`, `ui.density` and `ui.surfaces` profile keys, settable through
  `prefs set`.
- **App window.** The Chrome `--app` launcher (D10), using a dedicated profile under
  `<data-dir>/ui/chrome-profile`.
- **`apps/web` skeleton.** Vite, React, TanStack Router and Query; app shell with top bar, Bindu,
  navigation, theme and surfaces applied from preferences, and a reconnect banner. Built and
  embedded into the CLI package.
- **Security suite.**

**Acceptance.**

- `yantra ui` opens the app window. A second `yantra ui` reuses the live host and opens a new
  window. `--print` and `--json` work.
- The full §10 security suite passes.
- A third run-class invocation queues until a slot frees; after a host restart, queued items show
  **Not started**.
- Killing the host mid-run leaves the worker running, and a new host reattaches.
- The app renders with no third-party network request (checked from the request log).

### FEAT-066: Read Surfaces

**Scope.**

- **Ledger.** History index plus file scan, with filters on outcome, mode, date and text. It shows
  live runs from leases.
- **Brief reader.** Rendered from `brief.json` (and `document.json` for template runs):
  - overview, key findings, sections (markdown, raw HTML off);
  - condition statuses, cited rows, Sources and Also consulted;
  - an EvidencePane that opens the quoted snippet for each citation;
  - captures and notices;
  - export of the existing files.
- **Audit.** From the audit builder: the trust narrative, model-bound versus local-only material,
  secret usage, and provenance as text.
- **Artifact registry.** Maps each run file type to a viewer, with raw fallbacks (JSON tree, text,
  image).
- **Instruments.** OutcomeBadge, RequirementList, ConditionTable, CitationChip, EvidencePane,
  CaptureGallery, ProtectedValue, EventInspector.

**Acceptance.**

- Every golden Brief in the repo renders.
- Every cited claim opens its evidence in one click (e2e).
- Every file in a sample run directory has a viewer or raw fallback.
- ProtectedValue never shows a value or its length.
- Outcome words match the CLI exactly.

### FEAT-067: Mission — Composer & Live Run Screen

**Scope.**

- **Composer.**
  - One input with modes Ask, Research, Do and Run (workflow picker).
  - Options generated from the registry for the selected command only, each showing where its
    effective value comes from.
  - Template selection.
  - `do` unavailable with reason and fix when no provider is configured.
- **Cockpit.**
  - Top bar: Bindu, mode, goal echo, elapsed time, BudgetGauges, Stop.
  - Understood panel: contract summary in the agent voice, ContractRing, RequirementList.
  - Engine panel: RunTimeline with steers, escalations and the current call.
  - CliTwin with Copy.
  - Glass over a neutral backdrop until FEAT-069 supplies the stream.
- **Queue.** Queued and stalled states.
- **Finish.** On completion a View Transition into the Brief.
- **Recovery.** **Resume** (workflow runs) and **Run again** (any run, prefilled from its
  `CommandInvocation`) from Mission and the Ledger.

**Acceptance.**

- A `research --no-llm` and a scripted fake-provider `do` show every `RunEvent` in an instrument or
  the inspector.
- The CLI twin, run in a terminal, starts the identical command.
- No option appears on a command that cannot act on it.
- Stop aborts cleanly.
- Reloading the window mid-run resumes the live view with no gaps.

### FEAT-068: Interventions & Notifications

**Scope.**

- **Model.** The `Intervention` model in protocol: kinds `consent | handoff | input | takeover`;
  lifecycle `raised → notified → answered | expired → resolved`; persisted to `interventions.jsonl`
  and `notifications.jsonl`.
- **MVP behavior per kind:**
  - **consent** pauses and continues on approval;
  - **handoff** is terminal, with `blocker`, `safestNextAction` and the recovery that applies;
  - **input** is recorded when a run ends partial on missing information, with the missing items, so
    the Inbox offers **Run again with this added** (composer prefilled, missing items highlighted);
  - **takeover** is defined in the schema, and in the MVP it resolves as a handoff.
- **GuardedSwitch.** Hold-to-confirm, Deny as default, remaining time shown. `ConfirmationDecidedBy`
  gains `user_app`.
- **Attendance ceiling.** Implemented exactly as §8 specifies.
- **Inbox.**
  - live interventions from all attached runs;
  - parked scheduled runs, resolved by running `confirm` through a worker;
  - expired and handed-off items with their recovery action.
- **`yantra confirm`.** Resolves a live run's consent over its socket.
- **Desktop notification.** The worker sends "needs you" through `SinkNotifier` whether or not a host
  is attached.
- **Bindu.** Turns Rani while the Inbox has open items.

**Acceptance.**

- A consent answered in the app records `user_app`, and one answered with `yantra confirm` records
  `user_cli_confirm`.
- With no host attached, the ceiling expires at 15 minutes (stepped clock), the run exits 4, and the
  item appears in the Inbox of the next host.
- Agentic waits never exceed `agent.confirm_timeout`.
- A parked scheduled run can be approved from the Inbox and then runs zero-LLM as today.
- A desktop notification is attempted exactly once per raised "needs you" item.

### FEAT-069: Live Browser View

**Scope.**

- **Task 1 — spike** (may start after FEAT-064). Stream CDP `Page.startScreencast` at 5–10 fps under
  four blurred glass panels. Measure frame time, CPU and sampled contrast in both themes, and set
  the budget and the automatic Solid threshold.
- **Then:**
  - a screencast of the **task page only** in the worker: JPEG, size-capped, acknowledged per frame,
    started and stopped on demand, never persisted, never sent to the model;
  - worker-side suppression under the sensitive-screen latch, shown as "Protected screen — hidden";
  - a headed-run state ("Running in a visible window") with a focus action;
  - a BrowserViewport instrument behind the cockpit HUD;
  - automatic Solid when frame time exceeds the budget;
  - the safety documentation update.

**Acceptance.**

- At least 5 fps with the app main thread under 15% of one core on the reference machine (recorded
  in the spike report).
- No frame is forwarded while the latch is set (test with a password-field fixture).
- No frame file exists in the run directory after a run.
- The headed state is shown for headed runs.
- Contrast on glass meets AA over the sampled backdrops, or Solid engages.

### FEAT-070: Parity Manifest, Command Palette & Generated Surfaces

**Scope.**

- **Parity manifest** in `apps/web`. It maps every registry command, `RunEvent` kind and artifact
  type to a surface or instrument, or to a written exemption (`--json`, `--open`, `open --print`).
  The parity test enforces it and empties FEAT-062's allowlist.
- **Palette.** `Ctrl/Cmd+K` reaching every surface and command. It accepts typed CLI syntax through
  `CommandInvocation.parse` and offers "Copy as command" on every result.
- **Generated surfaces.** Drshya forms and tables generated from the registry and each command's
  `--json` schema for:
  - Settings: Installation (`config`), Preferences (`prefs`/`profile`, with provenance), Models,
    Browser (install and update keep their explicit consent step), Sites, Data directory;
  - Workflows (`list workflows`, `show`, `lint`, run);
  - Templates;
  - Schedules (`schedule`, `schedules`, `unschedule`, daemon status);
  - Usage (table);
  - Daemon (`status`; `stop` asks first).

**Acceptance.**

- The parity test passes with zero unmapped entries and an empty allowlist.
- Every generated form submits a `CommandInvocation` whose CLI twin equals what a terminal user
  would type.
- The palette executes any typed command it can parse and explains the error for one it cannot.

### FEAT-071: Onboarding, Health & Credentials

**Scope.**

- **Onboarding.** First-run onboarding mirroring `init`: provider, credential reference, model,
  storage, search-provider key, and the sensitive-context grants, with explicit questions and no
  inference (memory: prefer explicit user grants). It is skippable.
- **Health.** `doctor` checks with status, detail and the engineered remediation for each (only
  moves the engine has a path for; memory → Coding Standards). Smoke checks run as a run-class
  worker.
- **Credentials.**
  - Names only.
  - Set and remove run in-process (D2), with a write-only field: the value is never displayed,
    echoed or logged.
  - Where a credential is referenced, the reference is shown with ProtectedValue.

**Acceptance.**

- Onboarding produces the same `config.yaml` and `profile.yaml` as `init` for the same answers.
- Every `doctor` check renders, with its remediation where one exists.
- The canary-secret test passes for set, list and remove.
- No credential value ever reaches the app after it is submitted.

## 13. Phase 2 (Deferred and Documented)

Each item lists what the MVP lays down so Phase 2 is an extension, not a redesign.

- **Live takeover** — for a captcha, login or multi-factor challenge, the run pauses with a
  `takeover` intervention. You solve it yourself in the live view (pointer and key input forwarded
  to the task page through CDP `Input.*`), press **Done**, and the agent observes the page again and
  continues. Yantra never solves or bypasses a challenge itself; a human completing it in their own
  browser is the sanctioned path (memory → General, challenge and no-evasion rules).
  _MVP lays down:_ the `takeover` kind, the run socket, the screencast, latch handling.
  _Needs:_ input forwarding, an agent pause/resume contract across a human action, latch rules for
  input.
- **`ask_user` for missing information** — a tool the agent calls when the goal lacks a required
  value. The run pauses with an `input` intervention and continues with your answer. Answers are
  treated like goal-supplied values: attested, sanitized, masked under the FEAT-FP-008 rules, and
  never secret-shaped literals (secrets go through credential references).
  _MVP lays down:_ the `input` kind and the "Run again with this added" flow.
  _Needs:_ a tool-catalog change and a prompt-version bump (memory: five places), plus masking rules.
- **Desktop notifications for finished or failed runs** — sent only when the app window is not in
  focus; "needs you" notifications already ship in FEAT-068. _MVP lays down:_ `SinkNotifier` routing
  and the intervention log.
- **Live view of CLI-launched runs** — CLI runs already serve a run socket (FEAT-064). This adds
  attach from the app, read-only first.
- **Target brackets on the live view** — needs a viewport-relative element box on `A<n>` action
  evidence (value-free, so FEAT-056 still holds).
- **Bespoke studios** — Workflow studio (natural-language YAML view, inline lint, params, locator
  candidates, `do --save-as` review); Recorder and web annotate (requires a `yantra record` command
  first; parity will force it); Schedules timeline; Template editor with live preview; Usage and
  cost charts; Provenance thread graph; Compact density across every surface.

## 14. Success Criteria

- The parity test passes with zero unmapped commands, event kinds or artifact types.
- A non-terminal user completes a first `ask` within two minutes of `yantra ui` on a configured
  install, and a `do` with one consent, without opening a terminal.
- Every cited claim in a Brief opens its evidence in one click.
- Killing any one process (worker, host or app window) loses no run data. The run either completes
  or ends with an honest outcome and a recovery action.
- The localhost security suite and the canary-secret scans pass on Windows, macOS and Linux.
- Event latency p95 < 150 ms; live view ≥ 5 fps within budget, or Solid engages automatically.
- All text meets WCAG 2.2 AA in both themes, on glass and solid.

## 15. Open Questions

- **Exact `RunEvent` field shapes for the deterministic `ask`/`research` phases** — FEAT-063 spec,
  keeping them bounded and sanitized like agent progress events.
- **Heartbeat and stall thresholds** (5 s / 30 s proposed) and **host idle exit** (10 minutes
  proposed) — confirm in FEAT-064 and FEAT-065 against real runs.
- **Edge as the UI window on Windows when Chrome is absent** (D10) — confirm `--app` behavior and the
  profile location per OS in FEAT-065.
- **Visual-regression tolerance across OSes** — font rasterization differs; FEAT-061 decides whether
  baselines are per-OS or Linux-only in CI.
- **Is the park → `yantra confirm` → resume flow complete?** `TODO.md` (FEAT-020 follow-ups, "Wire a
  real `ConfirmationGateway`") still records it as open: on re-entry the checkpoint builds a fresh
  `ConfirmationRequest` without looking up the prior grant. FEAT-021 later shipped
  `resolveParkedRun`, so the entry may be stale. **FEAT-068's spec must verify this first**, because
  approving a parked scheduled run from the Inbox depends on it. If it is still open, closing it
  becomes FEAT-068's first task.
